name: export
summary: Makes a variable visible to programs started from the shell.
description: Shell builtin. A plain variable (NAME=value) only exists in the current shell; export turns it into an environment variable, passed on to every program started afterwards. This is how you change the PATH or give configuration (an API key, a port) to an application. As with alias, the effect disappears when the terminal closes, unless the line is added to ~/.bashrc.

options.description: Removes the export attribute: the variable becomes local to the shell again.
Exports a shell function instead of a variable.

arguments.name: NAME=VALUE
arguments.description: Variable to export, with or without a new value. No spaces around the =.

examples.explanation: Programs that open an editor (git, crontab…) will use nano.
Adds a directory at the start of the PATH, so commands in it can be found.
Gives a configuration variable to an application.
Checks the exported value of PATH.
